findings.evidence: Lines 54–64 build `G` from `(baseChangeFunctor f).obj X`, while the same arrow construction applies directly to `X.obj.d₀`; roadmap lines 564–578 separately request the base-change functor and the matrix-factorization cokernel functor.
findings.fix: Define the direct cokernel functor on `MatrixFactorization T v` first, then define the base-change cokernel as `baseChangeFunctor f ⋙ cokernelFunctor` and formulate the projection/universal-property API from that decomposition.
findings.issue: `cokernelFunctor f` only constructs cokernels after `baseChangeFunctor f`, although taking `coker d₀` is already a functor `MatrixFactorization T v ⥤ FGModuleCat T`; this conflates two independent roadmap operations and forces even an unreduced cokernel through `f := RingHom.id`.

summary: The cokernel construction is tied unnecessarily to scalar extension instead of exposing the natural functor on matrix factorizations themselves.
